projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The sustained 16-20 device count paired with zero camera motion on a Monday evening strongly indicates a private gathering where guests are congregated in a camera-blind zone, with a recent spike to 19-20 devices suggesting the event is still active. This matters because it confirms the flagged correlation and highlights a monitoring blind spot during social events.

The persistent 16-18 device count combined with zero camera motion for over four hours on a Monday evening strongly suggests the home is unoccupied, with the device count likely driven by smart home infrastructure or electronics left on rather than active occupancy.

The sustained 16-19 device count with zero camera motion since late afternoon strongly indicates connected devices are parked outside (likely in vehicles) rather than inside the home, suggesting the family may still be arriving or devices are stationary in the driveway/garage.

The sustained high device count paired with zero camera activity past typical Monday return hours confirms the house remains unoccupied, and the absence of any recent device count increase or motion suggests the family is still out or delayed.

The sustained high device count (18-21) paired with zero camera motion on a Monday afternoon strongly confirms the house is unoccupied, likely with family phones left connected or smart home systems running; this warrants a quick verification to ensure security and prevent unnecessary energy drain.

The sustained 19-23 device count paired with zero camera activity on a Monday afternoon confirms the household is unoccupied, while the rapid device count fluctuations indicate recent departure or transit, warranting a quick security verification before they return.

The Monday afternoon timing combined with zero camera motion strongly suggests the house is empty, making the sustained 19-24 fluctuating device count a likely artifact of IoT devices or network instability rather than actual occupancy.

The sustained 20+ device count with rapid connection fluctuations and zero indoor camera activity on a weekday afternoon strongly suggests multiple vehicles with active Wi-Fi hotspots parked on the property rather than people inside. This explains the network load without triggering motion sensors and warrants a quick network security check.

The persistent high device count (20–24) paired with zero camera motion on a Monday midday indicates the house is likely empty, with presence data driven by stationary IoT devices or a network artifact rather than actual occupancy.

The rapid oscillation of connected devices (21–24) on a Monday midday, paired with zero camera activity, suggests either unreported guests or the children are home from school; this connection cycling may also indicate network congestion that could be impacting camera reliability.
